angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 699,874 km at 266.55 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.7516 +/- 0.0090 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 266.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.006 +/- 0.031 solar radii from Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract): 699,874 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.965 +/- 0.091 solar masses from Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5616 +/- 66 K from Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-19.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.417, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
